transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because I can’t really get past something I keep seeing on my face. It’s this rough-looking, kind of sunken patch, mostly on one side, and I notice it in the mirror and especially in photos. It makes that whole side of my face look old to me, like beat-up or weathered, more than it should.

People keep telling me they barely see what I’m talking about, or that it’s not a big deal, but I don’t know… when I look, it’s right there. I keep noticing it, and it’s been hard to just shrug off. I work construction, so I know I’ve been out in the sun and all that, but this feels like it stands out in a way I can’t stop seeing.
Can you describe exactly what you see on your face again—do you feel it’s something others would objectively see and comment on, or does it feel more like something only you notice or worry about?

Yeah, so… what I see is this rough-looking area, kind of like the skin is uneven or sunken in a little, mostly on one side of my face. It’s hard to explain without pointing at it, but in the mirror it makes that side look older to me, like worn down or beat-up compared to the other side. And in photos it’s worse, because once I see it, that’s all I can focus on.

As far as other people noticing it… that’s where I get stuck. People keep saying they barely see anything, or they say, “You look fine,” or they kind of brush it off like I’m making too much of it. So I guess objectively, maybe it’s not something everybody is walking around commenting on. But to me it looks obvious. Like, I feel like if I can see it that clearly, other people must be able to see it too, even if they’re being polite or don’t want to say anything. It doesn’t feel small when I’m looking at it.
Does this concern about your face cause you a lot of distress, or has it affected your daily life in any way, like making you avoid pictures, social situations, or other activities?

Yeah… it does. More than I’d like to admit, honestly. It’s not like I just glance in the mirror and move on. Some mornings I get stuck looking at it, trying different angles, checking if it looks worse in the bathroom light versus by the window, and then suddenly I’m running behind. I’ve been late getting out the door for construction jobs because I’m messing with how I look or just standing there staring at that side of my face.

And at work, if somebody wants to take site photos, like progress pictures or group shots, I try to dodge them now. I’ll say I need to grab something from the truck or I’ll stand off to the side, because I don’t want that side of my face showing up and then having to see it later.

It’s affected family stuff too. We do game nights sometimes, and I’ve skipped some of those lately. I tell people I’m tired from work, which is partly true sometimes, but really it’s that I don’t want to sit there under the lights with everyone looking at me. I know that probably sounds like a lot over one patch of skin, but when I’m thinking about it, it feels like everybody’s eyes go right to it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, camouflaging the area, or seeking reassurance, because of how you feel about that part of your face?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I don’t want to call it a routine, but it kind of has become one. Before work, especially, I’ll go into the bathroom and check it in the mirror, and then I’ll turn my face one way, then the other way, because depending on the light it looks different. The overhead bathroom light makes it look one way, and if I step closer to the window or turn my cheek, it can look worse, like more hollow or rough. So I’ll keep doing that, like I’m trying to prove to myself whether it’s as bad as I think it is.

And I catch myself rubbing at it, too. Not like I’m fixing anything, because obviously rubbing it doesn’t fix it, but I’ll touch it or rub over the spot like I’m checking the texture or trying to smooth it out. Then I’ll look again, and sometimes it just makes me more aware of it.

If I’m going somewhere like my sister’s game night, that’s when I get worse about it. I’ll check it a bunch before leaving, and if I think it looks too obvious under the light, I start thinking maybe I shouldn’t go. Sometimes I’ll wear a hat pulled kind of low, even indoors for a while if I can get away with it, just so that side of my face feels less exposed. Or I’ll make some excuse, like I’m beat from work, and not go at all.

It’s embarrassing saying it out loud, because it sounds like I’m spending all this time over a patch of skin, but yeah… I check it, mess with it, try to hide it a little, and sometimes I just avoid showing up if I can’t stop thinking about how it looks.
When you worry about that area on your face, is it mainly that you feel self-conscious, like others are judging you or thinking negatively about your appearance?

Yeah, I think that’s a big part of it. It’s like… I’m not just noticing the patch and thinking, “Oh, my skin looks a little off.” It turns into this feeling that if I can see it that clearly, then other people must be seeing it too, and they must be thinking something about it.

I keep seeing this rough, kind of sunken-looking spot on one side of my face, especially in photos or certain mirrors, and it makes that side look older to me—like beat-up or worn down compared to the rest of me. And then when I’m around people, I start feeling like that’s what they’re looking at. Even if nobody says anything.

The confusing part is people keep telling me they barely notice it, or they act like it’s nothing. But I don’t really believe it in the moment. I figure maybe they’re just being nice, or they don’t want to embarrass me. So yes, I guess it is self-consciousness, but it feels stronger than that—like I can’t stop seeing it, and I assume everyone else is seeing this ugly thing on my face too.
Has this concern about the appearance of that area on your face ever interfered with your ability to work, be around others, or carry out your usual daily activities?

Yeah… it has. I mean, I’m still working, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function at all, but it definitely gets in the way.

There’ve been mornings where I’m supposed to be heading out for a construction job, and instead I’m stuck in the bathroom looking at that spot on my face, turning my head, checking it, trying to decide if it looks as bad as I think. And then I realize I’ve burned through time and I’m late getting out the door. That’s happened more than once, and then I’m driving already stressed out and irritated with myself.

At work, it’s started affecting little things too. If someone wants to take site photos or group pictures, I’ll kind of disappear or make an excuse, like I need to grab something or go check something else. I just don’t want my face in the photo, especially from that side, because then I know I’ll end up seeing it later and picking it apart.

And socially… yeah, I’ve skipped some family game nights. I tell them I’m tired from work, and sometimes I am, but the bigger reason is I don’t want to sit there feeling like people are looking at my face under the lights. It feels stupid saying it, because it’s just supposed to be family and a normal evening, but it can feel like too much. So yeah, it’s interfered with work, being around people, and just doing normal stuff I used to not think twice about.
Can you tell me if your concern about that area on your face is mainly about how it looks, or if it’s more about how people might react to you or judge you because of it?

It starts with how it looks, definitely. I mean, the thing that gets me is seeing it in the mirror or in photos—that rough, kind of sunken-looking patch on one side of my face. It makes that side of me look older to me, like worn down or beat-up, and once I see it, I can’t unsee it.

But then it kind of turns into the other part, too. Because if I’m seeing it that clearly, I start thinking other people must see it, and then I wonder what they think. But the main thing, the thing I’m stuck on, is the appearance of it itself. I’m here because I just can’t stop seeing it, even though people keep telling me they barely notice anything. I hear them say that, but when I look in the mirror or see a photo, it doesn’t feel barely noticeable to me. It feels obvious.
Do you find that these thoughts about the appearance of that area on your face come up automatically or intrude on your mind, even when you’re trying to focus on something else?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually probably the biggest reason I’m here, honestly. It’s not like I sit down and decide, “Okay, now I’m going to think about my face.” It just kind of jumps in there.

I’ll be trying to do something normal, or even just catch myself in a mirror for half a second, and then I’m right back on that rough, sunken-looking patch on one side of my face. Or I’ll see a photo and it’s like my eyes go straight to it before I even look at anything else. I don’t see the whole picture, I just see that part, and then I start thinking that side of me looks old or beat-up. Like it doesn’t match the rest of my face.

And I know people keep saying they barely notice anything, and I’ve heard that more than once, but it doesn’t really land for me. Because when I see it, it feels obvious. So yes, the thoughts come up automatically. I can be trying to focus on something else, and it’s still there in the back of my mind, like I can’t stop seeing it.

When you think about how that area of your face looks, do these concerns feel specific to just that patch of skin, or do you worry more broadly that people might judge your overall appearance in social situations?

It’s more specific to that patch, honestly. I mean, I don’t love getting judged in general—nobody does—but the thing that grabs me is that one area on my face. That rough, kind of sunken-looking spot. It’s like my eyes go right to it in the mirror or in a photo, and then I can’t see anything else normally.

It makes that side of my face look old to me, or beat-up, like it doesn’t match the rest of me. And I know people say they barely notice it—my family’s said that, other people have tried to reassure me—but it doesn’t feel that way when I’m looking at it. It feels really obvious to me.

So it’s not like I walk into every social situation thinking my whole appearance is terrible from head to toe. It’s more that I’m worried that this one patch is what stands out, and then I start thinking, “If I can see it this clearly, they must be seeing it too.” But the main thing is the patch itself. That’s what I can’t stop seeing.

When you’re worried about how that patch on your face looks, do you feel driven to do something specific—like checking the mirror repeatedly, touching the area, or adjusting your appearance—to try to feel better or make sure it’s not noticeable?

Yeah… I do. More than I’d like to admit, honestly.

Before work, especially, I’ll get stuck in the bathroom mirror. I’ll be standing there when I should already be getting my boots on or getting out the door, and I’ll turn my face one way, then the other, because it looks different depending on the light. Like under the bathroom light it can look one way, and then if I lean toward the window or turn my head, I’m trying to see if that patch looks as rough or sunken as I think it does. I’ll tell myself I’m just checking once, but it turns into checking again and again.

And I do touch it, too. I’ll rub at it, like somehow I’m going to smooth it out or make it look less noticeable, even though I know that probably doesn’t really do anything. It’s just this urge, like I need to feel what it’s doing or make sure it hasn’t gotten worse.

It happens before social things too. Like my sister has game nights sometimes, and before going over there I’ll do the same thing—mirror, different angles, different lights. Sometimes I’ll put on a hat and wear it low, not even because it fully covers it, but because it makes me feel like maybe attention won’t go right to that side of my face. And if I look in the mirror and it seems too obvious that day, I’ve made excuses not to go. I’ll say I’m tired or I’ve got something else to do, but really it’s because I can’t get past how it looks.
Do you believe this rough, sunken patch on your face is the result of a medical or skin condition, or do you think it’s just normal variation in your appearance that others don’t really notice?

I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean… part of me wants to say it must be something with the skin, because when I look at it, it doesn’t just look like “normal variation” to me. It looks rough, and kind of sunken, like that one side of my face has aged differently or got worn down somehow. Like it looks old and beat-up compared to the rest of me.

But then people keep telling me they barely notice anything. And I’ve heard that enough times that I guess I know, on some level, maybe it’s not some obvious medical thing the way it feels to me. I don’t have people reacting like, “What happened to your face?” or anything like that. It’s more that I can’t stop seeing it. In photos, in the mirror, especially if the light hits it a certain way, my eyes go right there and it feels like the only thing I can see.

So… I don’t know if I’d say I’m convinced it’s a skin condition. I just know it doesn’t look normal to me when I see it. Other people say they barely notice it, but to me it stands out immediately, and that’s why I’m here. I can’t get past that patch.

When you look at that patch on your face, do you believe it is a real physical defect or skin condition that others should also be able to see, or do you think it’s more about how you’re perceiving it even if others don’t notice anything wrong?

I guess that’s the part I keep going back and forth on. When I’m looking at it, it feels real. It doesn’t feel like I’m imagining it. I can see that rough, kind of sunken-looking patch, and to me it makes that side of my face look older, like worn down or beat-up compared to the other side.

But then… people keep telling me they barely notice anything, and I know they’re not all lying to me. So maybe it’s more about how I’m seeing it, or how stuck I get on it. I don’t know. I’m here because I can’t stop seeing it—in the mirror, in photos, anywhere I catch my face a certain way. My eyes just go right to that spot, and once I see it, it’s like the rest of my face doesn’t matter anymore.

So I don’t know if I’d say others “should” be able to see it the way I do. I just know it feels obvious to me, even when everyone else says it’s barely there.

patient.answer:
Yeah… definitely. That’s actually probably the biggest reason I’m here, honestly. It’s not like I sit down and decide, “Okay, now I’m going to think about my face.” It just kind of jumps in there.

I’ll be trying to do something normal, or even just catch myself in a mirror for half a second, and then I’m right back on that rough, sunken-looking patch on one side of my face. Or I’ll see a photo and it’s like my eyes go straight to it before I even look at anything else. I don’t see the whole picture, I just see that part, and then I start thinking that side of me looks old or beat-up. Like it doesn’t match the rest of my face.

And I know people keep saying they barely notice anything, and I’ve heard that more than once, but it doesn’t really land for me. Because when I see it, it feels obvious. So yes, the thoughts come up automatically. I can be trying to focus on something else, and it’s still there in the back of my mind, like I can’t stop seeing it.

It’s more specific to that patch, honestly. I mean, I don’t love getting judged in general—nobody does—but the thing that grabs me is that one area on my face. That rough, kind of sunken-looking spot. It’s like my eyes go right to it in the mirror or in a photo, and then I can’t see anything else normally.

It makes that side of my face look old to me, or beat-up, like it doesn’t match the rest of me. And I know people say they barely notice it—my family’s said that, other people have tried to reassure me—but it doesn’t feel that way when I’m looking at it. It feels really obvious to me.

So it’s not like I walk into every social situation thinking my whole appearance is terrible from head to toe. It’s more that I’m worried that this one patch is what stands out, and then I start thinking, “If I can see it this clearly, they must be seeing it too.” But the main thing is the patch itself. That’s what I can’t stop seeing.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I do. More than I’d like to admit, honestly.

Before work, especially, I’ll get stuck in the bathroom mirror. I’ll be standing there when I should already be getting my boots on or getting out the door, and I’ll turn my face one way, then the other, because it looks different depending on the light. Like under the bathroom light it can look one way, and then if I lean toward the window or turn my head, I’m trying to see if that patch looks as rough or sunken as I think it does. I’ll tell myself I’m just checking once, but it turns into checking again and again.

And I do touch it, too. I’ll rub at it, like somehow I’m going to smooth it out or make it look less noticeable, even though I know that probably doesn’t really do anything. It’s just this urge, like I need to feel what it’s doing or make sure it hasn’t gotten worse.

It happens before social things too. Like my sister has game nights sometimes, and before going over there I’ll do the same thing—mirror, different angles, different lights. Sometimes I’ll put on a hat and wear it low, not even because it fully covers it, but because it makes me feel like maybe attention won’t go right to that side of my face. And if I look in the mirror and it seems too obvious that day, I’ve made excuses not to go. I’ll say I’m tired or I’ve got something else to do, but really it’s because I can’t get past how it looks.
